chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud, from Al Asbagh who said:

Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: Patience is of two types: patience during the calamity is good and beautiful; but better than that is patience when abstaining from what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prohibited upon you. And Remembrance is of two types: the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, during the calamity; but superior to that is the remembrance of Allah when abstaining from what He has prohibited upon you, thus it serves as a barrier.

key_terms.الصَّبْرُ: Patience, perseverance in the face of difficulty or prohibition

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between basic patience and superior patience in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguishes between two levels of patience and remembrance of God, elevating the higher virtue from mere endurance of calamity to active restraint from divine prohibitions. This distinction highlights the practical application of sabr as a protective barrier against sin, a concept central to Shia ethical theology. The hadith underscores that true spiritual excellence lies in maintaining God-consciousness during the struggle to avoid what is forbidden, rather than solely during times of passive suffering.

en.hubeali: Muhamad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud, from Al Asbagh who said,

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The patience is of two (types of) patience – patience during the difficulties is good, beautiful; but (even) better than that is the patience during (abstaining from) what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Prohibited upon you. And the Remembrance is of two (types) of Remembrances – The mentioning of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic during the difficulties; but (even) superior than that is the mentioning of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> during what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Prohibited upon you. Thus it (the patience) serves as a barrier’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Sinan form abu al-Jarud from al-Asbagh who has said the following: “

Amir al-Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib) (a.s.) has said, ‘There are two kinds of patience: to exercise patience in hardship which is good and graceful, yet better than this is to exercise patience against the temptation of committing what Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has prohibited one from doing. There are two ways of speaking of Allah: to speak of Allah the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, in suffering hardship, yet better than this is speaking of Allah (remembering Him) when facing temptation to commit what Allah has prohibited one from doing and one’s patience serves as a barrier.’”
